added_lemmas.gap: Generic finite canonicalization and polynomial optimization do not themselves provide this explicit at-most-eight-point, source-preserving certificate with null-stratum branches.
added_lemmas.consumer: This theorem supplies the common-SCM attainment step for the closed-simplex compatibility frontier, sharp interval, rational endpoint certificates, and constant-time procedure.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The previous handle described a search and did not specify responses on zero-mass strata or null experimental rows.  The corrected construction gives the ordered-threshold model with explicit zero-denominator branches.

The endpoint generator must avoid dividing by zero on support faces.  Feasibility forces every zero-stratum numerator to vanish, so assigning its unused response probability to zero preserves exact rational certificates.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The closed-simplex construction introduces the stratum masses, marginal probabilities, treatment assignments, and returned SCM candidate into the handle, so its free-symbol closure must be replaced atomically with its construction.

The interior-only theorem is strictly subsumed by the proved closed-simplex theorem.  Replacing the node is the schema-valid way to strengthen its scope while mechanically migrating every inbound dependency.

prose_updates.tldr: For the fixed binary collider with two mutually independent shared roots and private outcome noise, arbitrary normalized experimental tables are compatible exactly when \(-(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r)\), and the all-zero joint-intervention risk has the proved sharp interval \([\max\{a,b,a+b-pr\},\min\{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)\}]\).  One ordered-threshold private root with at most eight support points realizes every interval value while reproducing both complete tables, including all structural-zero faces.  The result yields constant-time endpoints, exact rational endpoint certificates, and a conservative optional sampling interval for this graph and intervention menu.

project_justification.fill: The project derives the two-mass fiber, proves a closed-simplex source-preserving threshold lift with explicit null-stratum branches, and packages the resulting iff test and max/min interval as an exact analytic certificate procedure.  For this fixed input and query the certificate can replace a call to Autobounds' generic polynomial optimizer, while Duarte et al.'s graph-general sharp-optimization theorem remains broader and is not claimed as a new contribution here.

sampling_model.overlap: No positivity or overlap condition is imposed on the population tables: normalization gives \(0\le a\le p\le1\) and \(0\le b\le r\le1\).  On any stratum with zero probability, feasibility forces its target-success numerator to zero and the construction assigns the unused conditional response arbitrarily.

prose_updates.related_work: Gresele et al. formulate structural causal marginal compatibility and explain why overlapping reports must share one response-function law.  Duarte et al., JASA 2024, prove that finite discrete causal bounds with observational or experimental constraints and product disturbance probabilities can be obtained sharply by generic polynomial optimization; their scope permits categorical laws on support faces.  The present result is a closed-simplex analytic specialization for one binary collider, two interventions, and one risk: it derives the compatibility inequality, closed-form endpoints, and small common-SCM certificates rather than strengthening the graph-general solver theorem.  Autobounds is therefore the same-input software consumer whose generic optimization can be replaced by this certificate on the stated specialization.  Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide graph-preserving finite canonical SCM representations, but not this eight-point menu-specific lift or formula.  Sachs et al. give symbolic response-function bounds under linear constraints, while the independent latent-source factorization here must be preserved explicitly.  Zaffalon et al., IJAR 2023, provide adjacent multi-source approximate inner bounding through causal EM rather than the exact compatibility and sharp closed-form result proved here.  Shridharan and Iyengar, Finkelstein and Shpitser, and Balke and Pearl provide related optimization, logical-bound, and response-type machinery, but no checked result among them states this fixed collider formula.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The universal source-preserving extension is proved for arbitrary normalized tables, including degenerate treatment marginals and zero-mass natural-treatment strata.  Its product-root assumption remains load-bearing: allowing a root shared by \(X\) and \(Z\), or otherwise correlating \(U0\) and \(V0\), can move the target outside the independent-source interval.  The at-most-eight-point private-root bound is a constructive upper bound, not an optimal-support theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved result concerns only the fixed binary graph \(X\to Y\leftarrow Z\) with the two stated independent shared roots, private outcome noise, the two complete intervention tables, and the risk under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0,Z=0)\).  Structural zeros are included.  A strictly positive-width conclusion is valid only under the additional interior condition \(0<p,r<1\); support faces may point-identify the risk.  Correlated or dependence-budget shared roots, different study populations, a simultaneous region for all four joint-intervention risks, three or more parents, minimal support, tie-optimal inference, a general thicket compiler, and any field-tier claim remain outside scope.  If regime \(B\) is omitted, the mass accounting gives \(q\in[a,a+1-p]\); symmetrically, omitting regime \(A\) gives \(q\in[b,b+1-r]\).
